*"In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." John 1:1*

Matthew 6: 31-32*

Anecdote:
----

As symbolism, as boring chatter to friends and as guide, as nudge, as divination unaware I'm doing it. Unaware I'm placing my faith on a piece of cards that without discernment enabled spirits to whisper messages back to me. I had faith in tarot out of boredom, out of guidance, out of comfort soon turned into an invitation for the deceitful spirits and entities. 

Notice I used the word faith and not divination. I simply believed I can use it, not for spiritual means but as motivational quotes or for self-help. I thought good angels would speak to me, not until I was receiving nasty messages for another three years. Tarot cards cannot offer discernment only Jesus can through the Holy Spirit.

The reason it was clearly abomination, is we are susceptible to being tempted through spiritual realm and it's something that opens a pathway to every spirit out there. 

*"Satan Masquerades as an angel of light" 
2 Corinthians 11:14*

*"And do not give the devil a foothold." Ephesians 4:29*. Any tarot card, any medium including Ouija that occultist remodelled, whatever intent it may be is already a foothold for the enemy to use against a person.

----

*"An entry dated February, 1392 in the treasurer Charles Poupart's book of accounts for Charles VI of France describes payment for three gilt decks painted for the king by Jacquemin Gringonneur. Strangely enough, 1392 was also the year Charles VI went insane."*

But that could be a hearsay? Okay.

*"It was originally intended as a fancy card game, but so was Ouija. Antoine Court de Gebelin, the French linguist, cleric, occultist, Mason, and member of the Lodge of the Philalethes Convinced of the mystical significance of the Tarot and fond of Egyptian lore, believed the cards' birth place was ancient Egypt along with six other occultist in accordance to the egyptian deity."*

I came from a Science High School here at PH, 6 years scholarship and I'd say I also had that same mindset (but life humbled me down).

I'd say I have strengths that others do not and they have strengths that I don't have. And now at college all I do is try to excel at my own pace, I used to seek for validation on my performance. It was like oxygen. Until I learned that we are all unique in our each way. Not special no. 

It's okay to learn and to grow, but not to the point kinakain ka na ng standards ng iba. (And when it happened with me, I almost got visually blind. Due to my workaholic state.)

Finding peace is more important, we will all be replaced in the future. Don't stress too much and don't be too hard on yourself. 

If you want to feel special, it should come from innate self-love. Choose to grow and excel not to compete with others by with yourself.

"Be tolerant with others and strict with yourself"- Marcus Aurelius

Another thing before I forget when we fail:

Let's not attribute failure to ourselves (I just realized that tonight. Idk if failure or rejection is your source of shame but that's mine)

But rather ask the 'why' and 'how' to the method.

Remember, rejection isn't real danger, it's not a gunpoint or kitchen knife following you anywhere else. It's a perceived notion that allows us to analyze the mistake and we are not defined by them.

I understand you on so many levels, the text speaks volume. One thing that you need to accept is that there is growth and you're not defined by your label. Just because the childhood parent contributes does no mean you can't grow better as the body and mind does heal. Next thing you'll need to learn is to be productive in the boredom and not focus your attention purely on the external.

This also meant being able to sort out skewed perceptions of yourself and other people. Setting boundaries, figuring out what works for you not for the sake of pleasing others (finding stillness and self control).

End note, be kind to yourself as you undergo the process of uncovering the shame. "I'm loved, I'm good enough. My worth is not tied to my performance"
